findings.title: The raw SendGrid client used for cancellation is never authenticated
findings.body: This handler only calls `sgMail.setApiKey`, but the newly added cancellation path uses the separately imported `@sendgrid/client` instance at line 57. `sgMail` configures its own client instance and does not configure this exported raw client. Consequently the POST to `/v3/user/scheduled_sends` will be unauthorized/fail, the catch block will swallow the error, and the cancelled reminders will remain scheduled in SendGrid and still be delivered. Configure this client with `client.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` before making raw client requests.

findings.title: Normal reschedules still create immediate SendGrid cancellation entries
findings.body: The primary booking-reschedule flow passes `true` as `immediateDelete`, causing `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` to immediately POST `status: "cancel"` to SendGrid instead of marking the reminder as cancelled for the cron job. These cancelled scheduled-send entries remain counted by SendGrid until their send date, which is the capacity limit this PR is intended to avoid; after 100 pending cancellations, later reschedules can again fail to cancel and send stale reminders. This path should use the deferred cancellation mechanism (and preserve the reminder row for the cron), rather than `immediateDelete`.

findings.title: One failed cancellation prevents all later reminders from being cancelled
findings.body: All SendGrid cancellations are performed inside one try block. If `client.request` fails for any reminder, execution exits the loop immediately and no later reminders are cancelled during that run. Since the initial cleanup deletes email reminder rows once their scheduled date has passed, reminders skipped near their send time can lose their cancellation marker without ever having been cancelled at SendGrid, allowing them to be delivered. Handle failures per reminder (and retain failed rows for retry) rather than aborting the entire batch.

findings.title: Reminder cancellation writes are fired without awaiting completion
findings.body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async, but are invoked from `forEach` and their promises are discarded. The cancellation handler can return successfully before the email reminder has been marked `cancelled` (or an unscheduled/SMS reminder has been deleted). In a serverless/request-scoped runtime those unawaited operations may be interrupted after the response, leaving reminders active and allowing cancelled-booking notifications to send. Collect and await these promises before completing the handler.
